description: The theme as composed.
Melody clarinet -> violin, accompaniment piano -> harp. Notes identical.
Tempo x1.3. Notes identical.
Whole passage down a tritone, the most distant key. Unchanged under key-relative coding; every node changes under absolute-pitch coding.
Parallel mode (major <-> minor). Scale degrees 3, 6, 7 altered; contour, rhythm, form and relations intact.
Passing tones fill melodic thirds; neighbor-note turns decorate long notes. Every structural tone keeps its onset.
Motif 2 in rhythmic augmentation (x2). Under scale-free rhythm coding only the duration relations change; under absolute coding node 2 changes as well.
Motifs 2 and 3 exchange places. Every motif identical; only temporal relations change (derivational ones such as 'a' is a sequence of a' survive).
Motif order reversed (4 3 2 1); each motif intact and played forwards.
Diatonic inversion about scale degree 3: the tonic triad maps onto itself, dominant and subdominant exchange. Harmony inverted with the melody.
Note-level retrograde: the whole passage backwards, melody and harmony.
